# North weekly 28 Sept 2026

Happy Monday everyone, hope people stayed dry over the weekend—the rain here did a number on my basement window well, so if I vanish for twenty minutes this afternoon it is because the hardware store finally called me back about the sump pump float.

Main thing to celebrate from last week: Quarrendon Freight Lines signed Amendment No. 3 on Sept 22, which puts them at 230 seats starting January 1. June Osei-Lark already got the countersigned PDF filed away on Wednesday morning, and Thea Ramaswell sent over a very nice note about how the second shift at their Eau Claire yard finally stopped keeping the backup paper clipboards by Door 14. It is always a massive relief to get the ink dry on Dana's biggest account before the October rush starts eating everyone's calendar. Dana is still chasing down one weird bug for them (ticket #PD-8841, the gate kiosk printer at their Duluth terminal cuts off the last two digits of the trailer number when a driver checks in with a 53-foot dry van), so if anyone in support sees that ticket floating around, please give it a nudge.

Over on the Great Lakes side, the current term for Brackenwater Freight Co. ends Nov 30. We are getting into the window where we need their winter dock schedule locked down before lake-effect snow starts messing up their cross-dock turns in Toledo. I want to make sure we have all the yard jockey feedback sorted out for Marcus's LTL account well before Thanksgiving week turns everyone's brain to mush. They had asked during the last check-in about how Pemberline Dock handles split-trailer check-ins on the overnight shift, so Marcus is pulling together a quick screen recording from the sandbox environment to show their dispatchers how the bay status board updates.

In other news, Tamsin Cold Chain had a minor panic on Thursday afternoon when a reefer carrier showed up three hours early at their Tacoma facility and the guard shack tablet froze on the temperature

# Subscription Agreement: Tansley Parcel

## 1. Parties and Record Dates

This Subscription Agreement is entered into by Pemberline Systems and Tansley Parcel for the subscription to Pemberline Dock described below. Pemberline Dock is Pemberline Systems’ yard and dock scheduling software.

This Agreement was drafted on 2025-01-08. This executed record was written on 2025-01-20. Both parties signed this Agreement on 2025-01-20. The effective date is 2025-02-01; the execution date and effective date are distinct.

## 2. Subscription and Term

Tansley Parcel subscribes to 110 seats of Pemberline Dock. The subscription is priced per seat per year.

The current subscription term begins on 2025-02-01 and ends on 2026-01-31. The end of the current term, recorded as the renewal date, is 2026-01-31.

The subscribed quantity shall be recorded as 110 seats in the subscription record, billing worksheet, and access-allocation register. Operational lists identifying users by shift or location shall refer to that subscribed quantity rather than treat each shift roster as a separate subscription.

## 3. Price and Discount

The price per seat per year is USD 1,800. A discount of 10% applies to the subscription.

For 110 seats, the annual amount before discount is USD 198,000. The discount is USD 19,800, resulting in a discounted annual subscription amount of USD 178,200.

The billing worksheet shall display the seat quantity, annual unit price, discount percentage, and discounted annual amount as separate entries so that Tansley Parcel may reconcile the invoice against this Agreement.

## 4. Payment Terms

Payment terms are net 30 days. Invoice preparation shall use the subscription particulars set out in Sections 2 and 3.

Procurement correspondence concerning invoice routing shall identify Tansley Parcel by its full name. Lev Arkadin, Procurement lead, is the customer contact for the administrative exchange of billing instructions

# Central weekly — June 16

Written on 2025-06-16.

## Marrow Fieldworks — June launch

- Marrow Fieldworks goes live in 2025-06. This week’s work is focused on making the first operating shift straightforward: checking the appointment import, walking through an early arrival, and making sure the receiving desk can find the day’s exceptions without opening several separate views.
- Pree's dealer account needs one more rehearsal of the late-truck workflow before launch. The test should start with a driver arriving after the planned window and end with the receiving clerk moving the appointment without losing the original arrival note.
- The door labels in the rehearsal file still mix “Door 4” and “D04.” I have asked the implementation team to use the labels posted above the physical doors, then rerun the daily schedule export. This is a small cleanup, but it matters when a shift lead is reading a printed sheet at the desk.
- Next step: capture the revised rehearsal results in the launch checklist and keep unresolved items visible at the top, rather than buried beneath completed setup tasks.

## Tansley Parcel — amendment and follow-through

- The Tansley Parcel discount amendment was signed on 2025-06-10. June Osei-Lark has been asked to keep the signed copy with the contract materials and check that the billing handoff points to that version.
- Lev Arkadin recieved the follow-up note. The immediate task is to close the loop on the document exchange, not reopen the commercial discussion.
- The operations conversation remains separate from the amendment. Dispatch reported that a rescheduled afternoon collection was difficult to distinguish from the original booking in the exported schedule. We are assembling a reproduction using a booking moved between two windows on the same day.
- I will review the reproduction before it goes to support. Include the original window, the revised window, and the export timestamp so the team can compare the screen

- 30 Jan 2026 — I need the HR loose ends done today, not sitting in my inbox over the weekend. Dana Okafor is on leave from 2 Feb 2026 to 13 Mar 2026. I’ll keep the leave paperwork separate from the North team handoff.
